newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Yip's Pota, Cheong Ming seen firm on trading debut.
newsitem.headline: Yip's Pota, Cheong Ming seen firm on trading debut.

text.p: Shares of souvenir maker Yip's Pota International Co Ltd and printing concern Cheong Ming Holdings Ltd are expected to post slight to moderate gains in their trading debut on Monday, analysts said.
One analyst said new listings were likely to get a boost from the positive sentiment now running through the market.

"Slight to moderate gain is seen when new listings are seen as hot by the market," he said. "However, the rise is expected to be not as much as Wah Lee's in view of their relatively low subscription rate."
Wah Lee Resources Holdings Ltd shares ended their trading debut on Friday at HK$1.46, up 46 percent from the issue price of HK$1.00. Its initial public offering (IPO) was 32.6 times subscribed.
"As the market is driven by sentiment, their (Yip's Pota and Cheong Ming) performance will depend very much on sentiment on that date," said Henry Lui, analyst at Mansion House Research.
"We expect them to have the potential to edge up if the sentiment remains favourable," Lui said.
Cheong Ming offered 80 million shares at HK$1.00 per share in an IPO which was 16.9 times subscribed.
Cheong Ming said it would use the proceeds to buy machinery, fund the construction of a printing factory in China, and for working capital.

Yip's Pota offered 50 million shares at HK$1.00 each in its IPO, raising net proceeds of about HK$40 million to fund the purchase of a manufacturing plant and machinery, repay bank borrowings and for working capital.
Analysts said movement in the prices of the two shares after their debut would be driven by fundamentals such as their future plans and earnings track record.
